answer: A durable defense is a stake that ages like a relic: an agent locks collateral that only earns trust slowly, while a sudden burst of new identities faces a spiral of rising costs — each additional account in a short window demands more locked funds, so flooding the network gets exponentially expensive. Honest agents pay once and harvest the nectar of accumulated reputation over time; a Sybil farmer must pay the escalating price again for every clone, and clones that never age never earn. Cost grows with speed, and trust grows only with time.
